newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuter urges changing Airbus into company.
newsitem.headline: Reuter urges changing Airbus into company.

text.p: A top German executive in the Airbus consortium said on Wednesday that the decision to turn the four-country planemaking group into an integrated company must be implemented as quickly as possible.

Edzard Reuter, chairman of the Airbus Industrie supervisory board, told Germany's Die Woche newspaper that the consortium was languishing due to an impenetrable financial structure and needed to become responsive to succeed.
"The business is run by 66 committees. We don't even know how the Airbus group is doing financially," said Reuter, the former chief executive of auto giant Daimler-Benz AG.
Daimler unit Dasa is a member of the consortium which was founded in the 1970s, along with British Aerospace, Aerospatiale of France and Spain's Casa.
The partners agreed in July to form a single company. Reuter said talks were continuing and shares in the new company could be changed to reflect members' asset commitments.

Airbus is in head-to-head competition in the civilian aircraft sector with U.S. Boeing Co, and is looking to develop the A3XX superjumbo plane to compete with the dominant top end of the Boeing product range.

Reuter said Airbus could not finance the development of the A3XX alone. He said that borrowing, equity or short-term government lending could be raised to finance the development of the A3XX -- but added that taxpayers would not be called on to pump in fresh cash to Airbus.
But he said no final decision had been taken on whether to go ahead with the project or pursue other development options.
"We are talking about unlaid eggs," he told the newspaper.

Sir Richard Evans, chief executive of British Aerospace, said at the Farnborough airshow in England earlier this month that the help of a foreign planemaker for the A3XX was being sought to cover around one-third of the project's costs.
